headline: PM Tarique Rahman asks Malaysia to reopen labour market for Bangladeshi workers
summary: During his first overseas trip, the Prime Minister met with Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim to discuss worker welfare and bilateral ties.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Putrajaya to discuss the reopening of the labour market for Bangladeshi migrant workers.
Malaysia has restricted the hiring of workers from Bangladesh since 2024 due to reports of debt bondage and forced labour, leaving many workers stranded or exposed to deportation risks.
PM Rahman requested the regularisation of illegal workers and the repatriation of detained Bangladeshis, emphasizing the importance of remittances for Bangladesh's foreign exchange.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim agreed to take measures to ensure transparency in recruitment and protect worker welfare, stating that exploitation for company gains cannot be tolerated.
The two leaders also witnessed the exchange of agreements on investment promotion, cultural cooperation, and counterterrorism, and pledged to negotiate a free trade agreement.
This visit marks PM Rahman's first overseas trip since taking office, as he seeks to attract investment and strengthen ties with Asian partners, with a visit to China next.
caption:
Can the labour market reopen? PM Tarique Rahman has asked Malaysia to consider welcoming back Bangladeshi workers.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Putrajaya to discuss the reopening of the labour market for Bangladeshi migrant workers.

Malaysia has restricted the hiring of workers from Bangladesh since 2024 due to reports of debt bondage and forced labour, leaving many workers stranded or exposed to deportation risks.

PM Rahman requested the regularisation of illegal workers and the repatriation of detained Bangladeshis, emphasizing the importance of remittances for Bangladesh's foreign exchange.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim agreed to take measures to ensure transparency in recruitment and protect worker welfare, stating that exploitation for company gains cannot be tolerated.

The two leaders also witnessed the exchange of agreements on investment promotion, cultural cooperation, and counterterrorism, and pledged to negotiate a free trade agreement.

This visit marks PM Rahman's first overseas trip since taking office, as he seeks to attract investment and strengthen ties with Asian partners, with a visit to China next.

headline_marked: 54 injured, 18 missing after [[explosion at Qatar LNG site]]
headline: 54 injured, 18 missing after explosion at Qatar LNG site
summary: A technical accident at the Barzan gas supply facility in Ras Laffan Industrial City caused a fire and explosion on Sunday evening.
details: Fifty-four people were injured and 18 remain missing following an explosion and fire at the Barzan local gas supply facility in Qatar's Ras Laffan Industrial City on Sunday evening.
QatarEnergy stated that the incident occurred during the start-up of operations. Emergency response teams were deployed to contain the fire, which authorities have since brought under control.
Qatar's Interior Ministry described the explosion as a "technical accident" and assured the public that there is currently no threat to public safety.
The Barzan gas facility, which has a capacity of 1.4 billion cubic feet per day, supplies critical pipeline gas to local industries and the country's power generation sector.
The facility also produces ethane, condensate, liquefied petroleum gas, and sulphur for both domestic and export markets.
Ras Laffan Industrial City is QatarEnergy's primary site for LNG production and export, with a total production capacity of 77 million metric tons per annum.
The incident comes as Qatar's LNG export capacity was previously reduced by 17 percent due to damage to two LNG trains and a gas-to-liquids facility from strikes during the US-Israeli war with Iran.
caption:
54 injured and 18 missing. A massive explosion at a core Qatar LNG site has sparked a rescue operation.

Fifty-four people were injured and 18 remain missing following an explosion and fire at the Barzan local gas supply facility in Qatar's Ras Laffan Industrial City on Sunday evening.

QatarEnergy stated that the incident occurred during the start-up of operations. Emergency response teams were deployed to contain the fire, which authorities have since brought under control.

Qatar's Interior Ministry described the explosion as a "technical accident" and assured the public that there is currently no threat to public safety.

The Barzan gas facility, which has a capacity of 1.4 billion cubic feet per day, supplies critical pipeline gas to local industries and the country's power generation sector.

The facility also produces ethane, condensate, liquefied petroleum gas, and sulphur for both domestic and export markets.

Ras Laffan Industrial City is QatarEnergy's primary site for LNG production and export, with a total production capacity of 77 million metric tons per annum.

The incident comes as Qatar's LNG export capacity was previously reduced by 17 percent due to damage to two LNG trains and a gas-to-liquids facility from strikes during the US-Israeli war with Iran.
